scenes.title: Cold Open
scenes.narration: Every second, millions of invisible messages cross the world. But how does data actually travel? The answer lives in seven layers.

scenes.title: What is OSI
scenes.narration: OSI stands for Open Systems Interconnection. It is a conceptual framework created by ISO in nineteen eighty four. Think of it as the blueprint every network follows. It breaks communication down into seven logical layers, each with a specific job.

items: A conceptual framework, not a protocol

scenes.title: The Big Picture
scenes.narration: Think of it like sending a letter. Each layer does one specific job, then passes the result down to the next one. We will go from the top, layer seven, down to layer one. Ready? Let us dive into layer seven.

blocks.sub: Each layer does one job, then hands it down

scenes.title: Layer 7 · Application
scenes.narration: Layer seven, Application. This is where you interact. Browsers, email clients, games, apps, they all live here. Common protocols: HTTP for websites, FTP for files, SMTP for email, and DNS for names. It is the human friendly face of the network.

scenes.title: Layer 6 · Presentation
scenes.narration: Layer six, Presentation. This layer does three jobs. First, translate, making sure both sides speak the same data language. Second, encrypt, protecting data with S S L and T L S. And third, compress, shrinking files so they travel faster. Think J P E G, P N G, and M P four.

scenes.title: Layer 5 · Session
scenes.narration: Layer five, Session. It opens, manages, and closes conversations. Like a phone call. You dial, you talk, you hang up. It remembers who is talking to whom, and for how long, so data does not get lost between sessions.

items: Remembers who is talking to whom

scenes.title: Layer 4 · Transport
scenes.narration: Layer four, Transport. This is the workhorse layer. It takes data, slices it into segments, numbers each piece, and adds port numbers, so the receiver knows which app the data belongs to. Now, T C P is reliable. It handshakes, checks every packet, and retransmits lost ones. U D P is fast. It fires packets and does not check, perfect for video and gaming. This layer is the difference between just send it, and make sure it arrives.

scenes.title: Layer 3 · Network
scenes.narration: Layer three, Network. This is where I P addresses live. Every packet gets a from and to address, like a postal envelope. Routers read those addresses and decide the best path, hop by hop, across cities, countries, and oceans. It is basically G P S for data.

items: IP addresses: a from and a to, like an envelope

scenes.title: Layer 2 · Data Link
scenes.narration: Layer two, Data Link. It packages data into frames, and adds MAC addresses, the physical, hardware I D baked into every network card. Switches live here, moving frames within a local network. It also detects errors, so bad data never reaches the layers above.

scenes.title: Layer 1 · Physical
scenes.narration: Finally, layer one, Physical. Raw bits, sent through cables, fiber, or Wi Fi. Electrical pulses. Light beams. Radio waves. This is where ones and zeros meet the real world.

blocks.sub: Where ones and zeros meet the world

scenes.title: Encapsulation
scenes.narration: Here is the magic. This is called encapsulation. As data travels down, each layer wraps it with its own header, like nesting dolls. By layer one, it is a fully packaged packet, ready to travel. On the receiving end, the process reverses. Each layer strips its own header off, going up, until the original data is revealed.

blocks.sub: Nesting dolls, all the way down

items: Down: each layer wraps it with its own header
Up: each layer strips its header off

scenes.title: Mnemonic
scenes.narration: Here is how to memorize it. Top to bottom: All People Seem To Need Data Processing. Bottom to top: Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away. Pick your favorite. You will never forget the layers again.

blocks.phrase: All People Seem To Need Data Processing
Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away

scenes.title: Real World
scenes.narration: Let us put it all together. You send a message. It drops through all seven layers on your device, crosses the internet, routers, cables, satellites, and climbs all seven layers back up on the receiving end. In under one hundred milliseconds.

blocks.sub: Down seven, across the world, up seven

scenes.title: Outro
scenes.narration: That is the OSI Model, the backbone of every network on Earth. Seven layers. One language. Now you know how data really travels. If this helped, subscribe for more tech explained simply. See you in the next one.

blocks.sub: Now you know how data really travels.
